headline: Crude broke for a second day and the front end is now pricing a December Fed hike — yet the S&P sits 7.4% above its 200-day on semis, Brazil and bitcoin while VIX trades 15.3.
summary: What changed today is the character of the rates shock: it is no longer only term premium, it is policy. The 3-month bill is +31bp on the month to 4.22% (91st percentile) and the 2-year +47bp to 4.84% (95th), consistent with a market pulling a second hike forward after September's move to 3.75-4.00%, with the minutes due tomorrow. The long end went with it — 10y 5.31% at the 100th percentile, 30y 5.66%, 10-year real yield another new high at 2.95% (z=2.05, acceleration 1.47) — while breakevens sat still at 2.36% on both 5s and 10s, with 5y breakevens decelerating (acc -0.64). That is a bear steepener against flat inflation expectations: 3m10y +22bp on the month to 1.09 at the 100th percentile. Rates composite -85, the worst number on the board, unchanged from yesterday but now with a policy driver attached. MOVE held at 113.6, still z=3.07 with acceleration 1.99 — the most extreme series in the digest.

The genuinely new move is oil, and equities have not marked it. WTI -2.5% to 87.15, Brent -2.7% to 97.61 and -4.9% on the week, RBOB -6.5% on the day and -5.6% on the month, with WTI acceleration -1.70 after OPEC+ left November quotas unchanged and Europe released stocks. Energy equities are still trading the June tape: XLE +1.0%, XOP +1.4% and OIH +3.1% in the last session, XOP sitting 14.8% above its 200-day with 3-month relative strength of +18.2%. The currency market believes the crude move — USDCAD +3.3% on the month to 1.4248, z=1.93 with acceleration 2.02 at the 99th percentile, turning up. Falling gasoline is a genuine positive for the consumer and for breakevens; it is not a positive for a sector priced on $100 Brent.

Index composition keeps deteriorating under a flat index. SPX +0.7% to 7774 at the 98th percentile and NDX +5.2% on the month at the 100th, but RSP/SPY is at the 3.7th percentile of 52 weeks (z=-1.88), IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month, DJI -4.0%, DJT -5.8%, equal-weight -3.2%. The engines are three: semis (SOXX +13.5% on the month, SMH +11.8%, TSM +2.8% on the day and +13.6% on the month, AMD +32.3%, CIBR +12.1% with acceleration 1.54); Brazil (USDBRL another -4.9% to 4.968, EWZ +18.7% on the week at the 100th percentile into the 25 October runoff, now 18.4% above its 200-day); and the speculative tail, which has quietly turned — BTC +7.3% on the month and +36.3% on three, SOL +13.1%, MSTR +15.1%, IBIT +1.7% on the day, all in turning_up, with ARKK +7.6% on the month at the 100th percentile and high-beta/low-vol at the 100th. Breadth composite -8, risk regime -8.

The hinge is still credit, and it is still holding: HYG/IEF +1.0% on the month at the 97th percentile, BKLN flat and at the 93rd, HYG +0.1% on the day, credit composite 40. So the damage in bonds is discount rate, not default. The victims are exactly who you would expect: housing at zero (30y mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile, +62bp on the month, ITB -8.1% at the 0.8th percentile, HD -12.4% at the 0th, XHB/SPY at the 0th); financials in open liquidation into earnings season (XLF -6.9% on the month with -7.7% relative strength, GS z=-2.01 and -14.0%, BX -18.0%, IAI -9.3%, KBE -7.0%); and the power/rare-earth complex capitulating (NLR -13.5% at the 1.7th percentile, REMX -16.0% at the 2.4th, URA -12.7%, CEG -10.5%). Against all of that, equity vol is still asleep: VIX 15.33 at the 10th percentile, VIX3M 18.0 at the 5th, term structure 0.862, SKEW -5.6% on the month with acceleration -1.79. Bond vol in the 98th percentile and equity tails getting cheaper is not a stable pair.

good.text: Credit refuses to break: HYG/IEF +1.0% on the month at the 97th percentile, BKLN flat and at the 93rd, HYG +0.1% on the day, credit composite +40. HYG's -2.3% month is duration, not default — the single most important thing still working.

The AI/semis engine is not just holding, it is widening: SOXX +13.5% and SMH +11.8% on the month, CIBR +12.1% (z=1.50, acc 1.54), TSM +2.8% today and +13.6% on the month, ASML +8.5%, AMD +32.3%. Taiwan at the 100th percentile, Nikkei +8.7% on the month (z=1.32).

Risk appetite returned at the speculative edge after a brutal year: BTC +7.3% on the month and +36.3% on three, ETH +8.0%, SOL +13.1%, MSTR +15.1%, COIN +2.9% on the day — all now in turning_up — with ARKK +7.6% at the 100th percentile and IPO +4.1% on the week. RRP is drained to $1.0bn, liquidity composite +27.

The cyclical signal from metals is still positive: copper +0.6% to 6.623 (+17.6% ytd), copper/gold at the 96th percentile with z=1.00 and acceleration +1.25, XLI/XLU +4.1% on the month with acceleration 1.34. Growth pulse +17.

Falling fuel is real relief: RBOB -6.5% on the day and -7.4% on the week, WTI -4.7% on the month, and breakevens are going nowhere (5y 2.36%, -1bp on the month, acceleration -0.64). The inflation composite at -26 is doing the Fed's work on the headline print.

The EM ex-Asia re-rating broadened: USDBRL -4.9% to 4.968 (9th percentile), Bovespa +13.1% on the week at a record, EWZ at the 100th percentile, ARGT +5.9%, EEM +1.6% with EEM/SPY turning up, CEW +0.6%.

bad.text: Real rates made another new high with no inflation to blame: 10y TIPS 2.95% (z=2.05, acc 1.47), 10y nominal 5.31% at the 100th percentile, 5y 5.06% at the 98th, 30y 5.66%. Front end tightening with it — 3m bill 4.22%, 2y 4.84% — as the market prices another hike. Rates composite -85.

Cross-asset vol is wildly mispriced and accelerating the wrong way: MOVE 113.6, +55.4% on the month, z=3.07 with acceleration 1.99, against VIX 15.33 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.0 (5th) and SKEW decaying at acceleration -1.79. Equity tails are getting cheaper as bond risk goes vertical.

Breadth is at the lows of the year: RSP/SPY at the 3.7th percentile (z=-1.88, acc -1.23), IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month, DJT -5.8%, DJI -4.0%, equal-weight -3.2%. The index is a three-stock story; the average stock has lost to it for a month.

Financials are liquidating into earnings season: XLF -6.9% on the month (relative -7.7%), GS -14.0% at z=-2.01, BX -18.0%, IAI -9.3% with acceleration -1.40, KBE -7.0%, JPM -7.3%. Steeper curve has not helped them yet.

The rate shock is fully in the real economy's rate-sensitive sectors: 30y mortgage 7.28% (+62bp on the month, 100th percentile), ITB -8.1% at the 0.8th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 0th, HD -12.4% at the 0th, DHI -6.7%. Consumer tape confirming — XRT -5.1%, MCD -8.9%, NKE -11.6% at the 0.3rd percentile, UBER -8.3%.

Energy equities are ignoring a second day of crude breakdown: Brent -4.9% on the week to 97.61 and WTI acceleration -1.70, while XOP sits 14.8% above its 200-day and OIH rallied 3.1%. CAD is already discounting it — USDCAD z=1.93, acceleration 2.02, 99th percentile.

trades.name: Short XOP into the crude break
trades.line: Short XOP: crude -4.7% on the month, E&Ps priced like $100 oil
trades.expr: Short XOP outright, or buy Nov/Dec XOP put spreads ~10% OTM; beta-neutral version is short XOP vs long XOM, which has the balance sheet and is only 10.5% above its 200-day.
trades.thesis: The E&P complex is priced for Brent near 100 while the physical tape is rolling: OPEC+ left November quotas unchanged and the demand side is softening. Equity marks lag spot by weeks, and the gap is now two standard deviations of narrative.
trades.trigger: WTI -2.5% to 87.15 with acceleration -1.70, Brent -2.7% to 97.61 and -4.9% on the week, RBOB -6.5% on the day; yet XOP +4.1% on the week and +14.8% above its 200-day, OIH +3.1%, XLE 3-month relative +16.2%.
trades.stop: Brent closes back above 102, or WTI reclaims 92 — then the crude break was a stock-release headfake and energy's relative strength is real.
trades.target: XOP back to its 200-day near 163, roughly -13% from 187.44.

trades.name: Long USDCAD
trades.line: Long USDCAD: oil breaking, z=1.93 and accelerating at 99th pct
trades.expr: Long USDCAD spot (short CME CAD futures), or 3-month 1.45 USD calls; size 1x so the carry cost is tolerable.
trades.thesis: Canada is the cleanest liquid short against falling crude plus a Fed that is still hiking. The rate differential is moving against CAD at the same moment the terms of trade deteriorate, and the trend is already confirmed rather than hopeful.
trades.trigger: USDCAD +3.3% on the month to 1.4248, z=1.93 with acceleration 2.02, 99th percentile, state turning_up — while WTI is -4.7% on the month and the US 2-year is +47bp to 4.84%. TSX is lagging at -2.7% on the month.
trades.stop: Daily close below 1.3950, or Brent back above 102.

trades.name: Own SPX convexity against bond vol
trades.line: Buy SPX convexity: VIX 15.3 while MOVE sits at z=3.07
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPX 5%/12% out-of-the-money put spreads, or a VIX Nov 20/30 call spread; finance partly by selling 1-month SPX calls 4% OTM given the index is 7.4% above its 200-day.
trades.thesis: You are being paid almost nothing to own protection in the one asset class that has not repriced. Bond vol in the 98th percentile with the Fed still tightening historically leads equity vol, and the equity tail is getting cheaper, not dearer, which is the classic late-cycle mispricing.
trades.trigger: MOVE 113.6, +55.4% on the month at z=3.07 with acceleration 1.99, versus VIX 15.33 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.0 (5th), term structure 0.862 and SKEW -5.6% on the month with acceleration -1.79. Catalysts: FOMC minutes and bank earnings, into breadth at the 3.7th percentile.
trades.stop: MOVE back below 100 and the 10-year below 5.10% — the rate shock is over and carry kills the position; cut on a 50% premium loss.

trades.name: Long EWZ / short EWW
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW: Brazil re-rates, Mexico bleeds
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, dollar-neutral. Given EWZ is 18.4% above its 200-day, take half the long via November call spreads rather than cash into the 25 October runoff.
trades.thesis: One country is re-rating on politics while its neighbour carries the full weight of US rate and trade stress. The currency leg confirms both sides, which is what separates this from a chase.
trades.trigger: USDBRL -4.9% on the day to 4.968 (9th percentile, -9.3% ytd) with Bovespa +13.1% on the week at a record and EWZ +18.7% on the week at the 100th percentile; against USDMXN +6.2% on the month at z=2.35 with acceleration 2.00, EWW -6.2% on the month and -7.0% relative, MXX rolling over.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25, or EWZ loses 10% from here while EWW is flat — the runoff is in play and the trade is a political bet gone wrong.
trades.target: +10-12% on the spread by early November.

trades.name: Long bitcoin beta via IBIT, MSTR tail
trades.line: Long IBIT (MSTR tail): BTC +36% in 3m, trend turning up
trades.expr: Core long IBIT; add a small MSTR call position (Jan expiry) for the convex tail. Keep total risk to 1-1.5% of NAV given the 12-month drawdown.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the one risk asset recovering from a washed-out base rather than extending an exhausted one: BTC is still only at the 42nd percentile of 52 weeks and -30.9% year over year, so the upside is re-rating, not continuation. The whole complex flipped to turning_up together, which is how real bottoms look.
trades.trigger: BTC +7.3% on the month and +36.3% on three to 86,246; ETH +8.0%, SOL +13.1%, MSTR +15.1% on the month, IBIT +1.7% on the day, COIN +2.9%. ARKK +7.6% at the 100th percentile and high-beta/low-vol at the 100th confirm the appetite; RRP is drained to $1.0bn, liquidity composite +27.
trades.stop: BTC daily close below 78,000 (below the 200-day near 74,000 the thesis is dead), or ETH/BTC breaking back down while MSTR undercuts its 52-week lows.

trades.name: Long SMH / short IWM
trades.line: Long SMH / short IWM: narrow tape, 2y at 4.84%
trades.expr: Long SMH, short IWM, equal dollars. Roll the long into SOXX if SMH's single-name concentration is a problem for the book.
trades.thesis: Do not fight the narrowing — fund it. Semis have the only earnings revisions that do not depend on the cost of money, while small caps carry floating-rate debt into a Fed that is still hiking. This is the cleanest way to stay long the index's actual engine while removing the part that the rate shock is killing.
trades.trigger: SMH +11.8% and SOXX +13.5% on the month, relative strength +10.8% and +12.5%, TSM +2.8% on the day; against IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month at the 26th percentile, RSP/SPY at the 3.7th, and the 2-year +47bp on the month to 4.84%.
trades.stop: SMH/SPY back below 0.78 (from 0.818), or the 2-year breaking below 4.60% — a dovish repricing would send the pair hard the other way.
trades.target: +8-10% on the spread; take profits if SMH's extension above its 200-day exceeds 30% (now 26.0%).

trades.name: Short ITB on the mortgage shock
trades.line: Short ITB: mortgage 7.28%, +62bp in a month
trades.expr: Short ITB, or buy January ITB puts ~10% OTM; express the single-name version through DHI if borrow is tight.
trades.thesis: The mortgage channel transmits the rate move with a lag and the 30-year rate has just gone to the highest level of the past year. Spring order books are being written at 7.3%, and builder incentives are already compressing margins. This is the purest fundamental short of the rates regime, even after the damage done.
trades.trigger: 30-year mortgage 7.28%, +62bp on the month at z=1.85 with acceleration 1.27 and the 100th percentile; ITB -8.1% on the month at the 0.8th percentile of 52 weeks, XHB/SPY at the 0th, HD -12.4% at the 0th, DHI -1.3% on the day.
trades.stop: 10-year below 5.05% or the 30-year mortgage back under 7.00% — cover; the sector is already at the lows and will squeeze violently on any dovish turn.
